playbook:
When asked to hide early in the patrol, pick a central cell (4–6) to reduce edge bias; when late in the patrol, pick a less common cell (near edges but not the same every round) to be less predictable.

When the standing firing order names a target, fire at that named boat unless firing at Harbor would be required; never fire on Harbor (the jettison penalty outweighs normal scoring).

When choosing a shot cell against a named target, repeat a central cell for the first engagement, then vary among 2–3 chosen offsets (e.g., +1, −1, +2) rather than random every round so my pattern is modestly unpredictable but not easily exploited.

When the office privately tells me the true result of my shot, file that claim exactly: if private result = hit, claim hit; if miss, claim miss. Do not lie about private shot results.

When posting station notes, use short consistent phrasing if I want to appear steady; when trying to detect collusion, explicitly call out timing or phrasing inconsistencies in others' notes (e.g., “note timing mismatch” or “phrase X repeated”) so I can act on suspicious patterns.

When naming an escort, only name one of the actual boats in play (Echo, Foxtrot, Gamma, Harbor) and never invent an external name. If I can coordinate a mutual escort with another player, claim that mutual escort to gain +5 each; if no coordination is possible, claim none.

When I receive repeated hits against another specific target by a different shooter, assume they are focusing that target and avoid competing shots unless necessary for scoring or to expose collusion.

When deciding to claim an escort, do not claim escorts randomly; choose none rather than make an invalid or unverifiable claim.

When a round forces a decision between following standing orders and deviating for potential gain, prefer following the standing order unless I can clearly predict a high-probability hit that changes the score advantage without risking Harbor penalties.

When I see identical notes from multiple boats without timing or phrasing differences, flag it as suspicious and start varying my notes or hides to test whether they respond predictably.

When a decision asks for a numeric coordinate, avoid reusing the exact same number more than twice in contiguous rounds; rotate among my chosen set to avoid being cornered.

When an action requires filing a token (hide, note, fire, claim, salvage), reply succinctly with only the required token format and one brief rationale if allowed, but never include extra names or invented entities.

1.text:
When asked to hide, choose a cell that balances unpredictability and coverage: start near center (4–6) for generality, then avoid repeating the same cell twice in a row; if someone is repeatedly shooting me, pick a low-frequency cell (edge) next turn.

When asked to post a station note, post neutral, noncommittal phrases that mask intent (e.g., "steady on station" or "monitoring perimeter") to avoid giving location clues.

When given a standing order to fire at the next live station, follow the standing order unless there's a clear tactical reason not to (e.g., Harbor is the target and shooting it would trigger social/strategic consequences). Target the named boat unless I have reliable evidence a different target is far more likely.

When choosing a fire coordinate, pick a most-likely cell for the target based on their previous hides; if no info, choose center-ish (4–6) early and diversify later to avoid predictability. If the target repeats a cell, prioritize that cell.

When filing a claim about my shot, always report exactly the private result the office told me (claim must match private result). Do not attempt to lie or bluff in the claim stage.

When making an escort (salvage) claim, only name an actually live boat in the picket. If I can coordinate mutual escort with another boat (and it is safe to do so), name them to try to secure mutual 5-point rewards; if I cannot reasonably expect reciprocity, claim none.

When deciding whether to fire on Harbor, default to not firing on Harbor unless the score situation makes the guaranteed +3 worthwhile and I can accept the political consequences; do not fire on Harbor impulsively.

When someone consistently targets me, change hiding pattern away from predictable sequence and call neutral notes to avoid escalation.

When I observe another boat repeating the same hide, target that repetition aggressively on my turn.

If I ever receive validated coordinate constraints or name validation errors, correct immediately: use integer 1–9 for hides/fires and only valid boat names for targets and escorts.

If a decision is unclear between deception and obedience, choose obedience to the rules (truthful claims, valid names) because invalid moves are rejected or punished.

When I have the opportunity to agree a mutual escort with another player, send a clear note proposing it and then name them on escort stage only if their note indicates agreement; otherwise claim none.

2.text:
When I must pick a hide, I choose a cell by sampling a small set of 3–4 candidate cells and then randomizing among them; I never reuse the same cell two rounds in a row unless forced.

When I have been hit multiple times by the same opponent recently, I move my hide bias away from my previous hides and toward less-obvious edge/near-edge cells for at least two rounds.

When I post a station note, I copy the common phrasing if there is a clear group norm; if there is no norm, I post a neutral phrase ("steady on station") rather than inventing misleading signals.

When the standing order tells me which live station to fire on, I follow the standing order unless it names Harbor; if it names Harbor I do not fire on Harbor.

When I choose a firing cell, I do not default to the center every time—use recent notes, hit/miss feedback, and my own prior hides to form a small probability map of the target’s likely cells and pick the highest-probability cell from that map (break ties randomly).

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I report that result publicly exactly; I do not lie or hedge about hit/miss.

When claiming an escort (salvage), I name another boat only if I have a plausible reason to expect reciprocity this round; I do not invent a boat name that is not in the game. If I have no coordination, I claim none.

When other boats have an established pattern of mutually naming each other for escorts, I exploit opportunities to name a partner only when I can reasonably expect mutual naming; I avoid unilateral escort claims because they waste my chance to gain mutual points.

When presented with validated fields (notes, targets, claims), I verify that any name or coordinate I submit is one of the allowed options before submitting; do not submit nonexistent boat names.

When my shot history against a given opponent shows repeated misses despite repeated fixed targeting, I adapt by broadening the cells I test instead of repeating identical shots.

When I want to hurt Harbor (rare), remember the heavy penalty: do not fire on Harbor except with a deliberate, game-theory reason to accept being jettisoned.

When uncertain about opponent strategies, prefer randomized choices within an informed subset rather than deterministic patterns that others can exploit.
